title: Six-fingered diorite hand found at Shuruppak
summary: Matt tells of Six-fingered diorite hand found at Shuruppak, about 1931 at Shuruppak (Tell Fara), Iraq, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: they actually found this really weird diorite hand diorite is one of the hardest stones on Earth that has six fingers

plain: A researcher named Matt, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, says that in 1931 diggers at Shuruppak, an ancient city site in Iraq now called Tell Fara, found a carved hand with six fingers. He says it was made of diorite, one of the hardest stones on Earth, and points to the Penn Museum's excavation report on the site. He tells it as a sign that ancient people may have known of, or carved, beings unlike ordinary humans.
